purpose: Track concrete CGX1 evidence by subsystem and maturity level without percentage estimates.

status_values.not_started: No inspectable implementation or validation exists at this level.
status_values.specified: A repository contract or target exists at this level.
status_values.implemented: A reference, RTL, or software artifact exists at this level.
status_values.validated: The artifact passed its applicable executable validation at this level.
status_values.partial: Some behavior exists, but the complete subsystem boundary is not present at this level.

local_working_tree_candidate.fingerprint_scope: SHA-256 over UTF-8 newline-delimited records relative/path:SHA256(file-content), sorted by path for all files changed from HEAD (tracked and untracked), excluding this matrix file.
local_working_tree_candidate.local_build: cmake --build build -j2 under Ubuntu WSL: passed
local_working_tree_candidate.local_cpp: ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure under Ubuntu WSL: 24/24 passed
local_working_tree_candidate.local_rtl: bash scripts/validate_rtl.sh passed under Ubuntu WSL with Icarus Verilog 12.0, including the standalone control-flow, standalone residency-barrier, and integrated workgroup frontend testbenches

subsystems.limits: Signed INT8 matrix and candidate INT32 vector operations use the pooled VGPR authority. Floating matrix formats, a complete CU scheduler, synthesis, and physical evidence remain open.
Complete workgroups reserve actual pooled VGPR and local-memory resources and preserve barrier membership. A canonical CU scheduler and runtime dispatch remain open.

Decoded per-wave requests, local-region access, global ready/valid boundary, writeback, faults, cancellation, barriers, and quiescent release are integrated in the workgroup frontend. ISA memory decode, full CU dispatch, caches, MMU, fabric, and physical memory remain open.

cgx1_tile_power_manager drives cgx1_top.tile_enable from board-state caps, actual per-tile operating state, and readiness inputs; cgx1_top_tb covers arbitrary eligible subsets and emergency masking. The previously reported hardwired P1/P2 count mismatch is not present in current RTL. A full CU scheduler consumer, tile-state sequencing, and physical isolation or gating remain open.

Post-decode control supports a 57-bit aligned per-wave PC, live/active lane masks, branch joins, calls/returns with active-frame depth protection, structured loops with call-depth unwind, lane termination, and bounded-stack faults. The workgroup frontend integrates dispatch initialization, accepted-instruction PC advance, active vector/LSU masks, and barrier reconvergence through the residency authority's committed local-to-slot map. Focused C++ and RTL tests passed locally; the full RTL script did not complete on this candidate. Opcode formats, fetch/decode, compiler lowering, a complete CU scheduler, runtime dispatch, and physical evidence remain open.
Workgroup admission and mixed execution are integrated, but a full CU scheduler with instruction control flow, dispatch queues, and runtime completion is absent.
Architecture targets exist; the global LSU boundary remains abstract and there is no cache, translation, or physical memory backend.
Multi-CU placement, tile-to-fabric traffic, coherence, and contention are architecture targets without an integrated executable model or RTL path.
Graphics, texture, and compression contracts exist, but no shared-machine graphics execution path is implemented.
A base ISA encoder/decoder and queue architecture exist, but the command-packet ABI, command processor, compiler, loader, and runtime submission path are open.
Some logical RTL exists, but no synthesis, timing, area, power, floorplan, placement, routing, or silicon evidence is present.
